After over 20 years of enjoying "just one more turn" I can confidently say I no longer wish to even finish the first age. This doesn't feel like a game. It doesn't feel like a smooth progression of a civilization. Instead it feels like a rough and grinding task-based checklist of requirements.

Gone are the days of doing your own things and playing however feels right. Now you are essentially punished for not following prescribed journeys through each win-con's specific flow chart.

The lack of advanced game settings leaves replayability extremely low - even with all these poorly provided mix and match opportunities with the leaders and different countries / regions. And the forcing of all players to meet in the first "age" before getting to the "far away lands" is atrocious...

This is the only Civilization game I have NOT had the PLEASURE of playing. I will throw a few more hours at it after each major update. Trust me when I say I want to flip the thumb to up - but I cannot. I will not. Not yet.

EDIT 1 @ 216 hours - It's definitely improving, but I still find myself enjoying Civ6 more. The added Mods from the workshop was probably the best improvement, which is sad that it had to come from the community and not the team. Anyhow, I will continue to play here and there after major updates. Until next time!

As a long time civ fan, and someone who bought the game upon release let me tell you- this game is NOTHING like the civ you know and love

Sure every civ game has unique gameplay --but at the end of the day this is truly not civ.

The ages are the absolute weirdest and most terrible decision they devs have ever made. It literally destroys the entire purpose of playing a full game through.

ALSO YOU DON'T PLAY AS THE CIV BASED THE PERSON YOU PICK. I know that sounds confusing but essentially if I wanted to play Himiko of wei (from japan) I would assume I'm playing as a japanese civiliation the whole time. BUT NOW- so building up a great empire doesn't even matter because you'll be playing as THREE different civilizations.

TLDR- don't get the game until they take ages out and admit they were wrong.
this game is so bad it is not even i have played ever version this one is trash as waste of money i wish i could get money back this is so bad omg so bad!!!
Wow.....what a let down, I will keep it short. I hate the fact that there are very limited races in fact everything is limited in this game.

People worry too much about the small things. As someone that does not have time to play 24/7 and critique every tiny aspect of the game I enjoy playing it a lot when I do have time. I have been playing these games since Civ 4 and this game certainly will not cause me to stop.

This game is a half-assed gong show. City state diplomacy and religion which have been key features in the whole franchise has essentially been lobotomized of any relevancy.

So you're telling me there is no absolute way for me to get suzerainty of this city state once somebody else claimed it? Bullshit.

You want to complement a religious playstyle with expanding wide? NOPE. You only get one era to play with it and you can't do shit with your opponents missionaries. 

This unfinished wreck of a game is an absolute travesty to the whole series with changes absolutely nobody asked for.
Why did you separate leaders and civs. What kind of logic is playing with Ottomans with a leader who is not a padişah. Nonsence!
I waited 9 years for this game and have only felt motivated to finish one campaign in the almost one year that I've owned it. At least the graphics are really good right guys?!?

I hate what they did the game. I feel rushed playing this game. The ages system is stupid and I hate it. The units don't look good, combat sucks. And diplomacy is very lacking. Gonna play 5 and 6 until 8 comes out in a decade.

Game stops at Modern age. Its like... half built... Buying the addons is like buying the pickles and onions individually at 1$ a pop for your already full priced burger. The game is fun enough to play for hours tbh, but it WILL crash, and the !!!auto-save feature does not work!!! So you will be at turn 160 and discover that unless you manually saved you have to go back to turn 30. There will be no warning for this. You are just no longer saving your game too bad for you. I will come back in a few weeks and try to enjoy myself again but I lost a marathon worth of progress... I was playing ALL day. I am a Sid Myers fan through and through, but if I wasn't I would demand a refund and never consider playing this game again.

Abysmal dogshit.
The game is unfinished, plain and simple.

-Mainline feature of Civ switching actively makes the game considerably worse.
-UI is cumbersome and looks like garbage, half the shit in it looks like placeholders.
-The way age transitions are handled is embarrassing, no gameplay designer would approve grinding the game to a screeching halt 3 times per run with a hard reset unless they were forced to in order to meet a deadline.
-The changes to tile improvements and buildings are whatever, a lot of seems arbitrary and just streamlining for the sake of it
-The only two additions I do not outright hate are generals and navigable rivers. That's not enough.

If you want to get into Civ, get the complete edition of Civ 5 or 6.
If you're coming from previous Civ games, wanting more 4X, try Humankind, It's Civ 7 with all the 'switch civs through the ages' thing except it's not a disjointed barebone unfinished mess that looks and plays like an early alpha.

The recent updates are a step in the right direction... there's a decent Civ game in there somewhere... maybe 3 years and $120 worth of DLC down the line but right now avoid like the plauge.

The game feels strange. There are many elements from CIV VI which are missing at a clear detriment to this title.

I originally purchased it near release and it was a horrible experience, quickly refunded. I recently picked it up again on sale and must say the game plays a lot more like classic CIV now but it has a lot missing. It doesn't really have that same draw as previous titles and feels lackluster...

If it had to be summed up, I'd say this feels a bit like a child between CIV V AND CIV VI that just never got any love in development. It seriously is lacking. CIV VI is still far superior, as is CIV V.

Its worth it at a cheaper price, the game is beautiful and well optimised. It is decently fun now. Not a truly bad experience. I cannot leave a negative review after seeing how much it has been corrected. Yet, my feelings remain super mixed.

Looks gorgeous.
Not fun.
Not intuitive.

I have hundreds of hours in Civ6, Civ5, and pretty much every other version. I've been playing civilization style games as long as I can remember. But this game just doesn't make sense.
Starting at pre-game setup - sometimes you select a leader and a civilization. Other times just one. No idea why.
Start the game and see a cool looking tile you want to build a city on? Cool, spend 3 turns getting there, only to have the settle button grayed out. No error message. No description of why. Restart game.

Stick with Civ6. I see literally no reason to want to play this version over the previous.

I'm not a fan of this game. It doesn't feel like a civ game. The era switching and leader switching is annoying. Limiting empire expansion is annoying. There's no thrill in the game to race for resources. The concept of towns reduces micromanaging cities but then they increased micromanaging by making me select each tile expansion spot. The pop ups asking me questions all the time also feel so annoying. I stopped reading them and just select which choice gives me what resource. It's overall an annoying tedious game and it's disappointing. It's not civ it's some mashup of something else that wants to be a controlled storyline based game rather than the excitement of a race between civs to the end. I don't recommend spending full price.

On launch, there were quite a few issues and gaps that should have been filled in prior to release.

However, over the last few months, the game has received a number of large patches and QoL updates that have brought it up to where it feels like a polished experience. Now, some of the most negative comments, right now, is that the experience doesn't seem to line up with the typical CIV experience. This is true, but I don't see it as a negative.

CIV has been around for a long time and I applaud the devs in trying a different approach, instead of just continuing to build on the same formula, even if it is tried and true. In this iteration, a full game of CIV is actually broken into three distinct smaller games, what used to be 'ages.' They're still called 'ages,' but they're fully unique game experiences in and of themselves.

This CIV update has also introduced a rogue-lite element, which I really enjoy. It's getting me to try new leaders and combinations that I wouldn't have tried in the past.

My recommendation: If you're into 4X and CIV games, give it a try. You may like it more than you expect.
If you're not into the old CIV games, definitely give it a try. It may have introduced the mechanics you felt were lacking.
If you're not into 4X or CIV, then I'd give it a pass.

The ideas for this game are interesting, but they are very poorly implemented, the age mechanic is far too destructive to the flow of the game.

I was going to wait a while to review, give them time to release an appropriate amount of bug fixing, etc, but now they've decided to add an even more expensive version of the game, the unfinished, unpolished game, and I am rather ticked off.

Firaxis, do better, Civ VII is a shameful release.

Released 3 dlcs when the base game isn't even enjoyable </3 

Civ 6 is so much better don't waste money on this.

Terrible compared to Civ 6. They needed at least another year of development before releasing.

A year later and the game still sucks.

Absolutely terrible. I've played every civ since the first one. This is unrecognisable. I held off buying it for over a year given the bad reviews. Eventually I gave in thinking it really couldn't be as bad as they said. I was wrong. Its a complete tragedy. Whoever signed off this awful product should be fired. I have requested a refund.
Now that you can play through as one civilization, it's a worthwhile upgrade to Civ VI (if you get it at half price).

We all know the base game launch of CIV 6 wasn't great but that pales into insignificance compared to this.

Basic features missing entirely, game customisation, auto exploring, queuing tech trees. Everything is a chore. The UI is hideous and looks like it was made for a tablet.

The leaders, civilisations and ages? You have taken a terrible concept from other games and brought them here. Gone are the days of being able to pick an empire and running it through all of history.

Why on Earth have you left out some of the most fundamental civilisations in history? Where on Earth is Britain?!

Having to rely on modders to fix your game that was clearly released a year two early. This inst a gameplay evolution, its a devolution to lesser games

I've been a fan of Civ since the very first one in 1992. Civ 7 is the worst in the entire series. I don't like the new combat system. You can't even choose a map of the real Earth. And I don't understand why you have to choose your leader from a different civilization. It's so bad that I only played for three hours and then reinstalled Civ 6, which I've already played for 500 hours.
It's like McDonald's replacing the beef in its Big Mac with chicken.

I am really disappointed that I pre-ordered this game. It is a far cry from the first six Civilization games, which I loved.
Not worth to buy, if you want real civilization game just buy CIV6. That full reset on age transit just kills the mood to continue...

Played it for free and it was a total waste of my time. Have played CIV since CIV II, this ain't it chief. Thanks for the confirmation that the series is dead.

The game is so trash they're letting us play for free and handing out DLC because the player base is too small to justify making more DLC for this game, but they are locked into this loser until CIV 8 (if it happens). Let the franchise die I say, it's over.

CIV 4 is still the GOAT. Don't @me.

they changed the game, and not for the better. they enabled winning conditions from the start of the game, but didn't give us an option to disable it till the final age. 
no matter what, the game now ends way before you reach the final age, basically making late game civ's obsolete.

Incomplete game. They charge you $80 for it and then another $30 for each DLC. The win conditions are confusing, and you don't seem to be able to win until the final age. This makes the early ages tedious, almost like something you have to power through with no tension or risk. Expansion is soft capped with limits to how many cities you can build or conquer, so expansion feels intentionally punished. Moving your pieces around difficult terrain that can be difficult to see feels cumbersome and more like work when you need large numbers of units to overcome enemy defenses (which honestly might just be a result of my being bad at the game). Overall, not very fun if you enjoy a conquest victory.

After 120 hours in this game and a lot of patience, I must not recommend it. I really wanted to. I have been playing since Civilization I over 32 years ago when I was a kid.

Beyond the millions of complaints of others that I agree with, and the near alpha release this game is in, I cannot in good faith recommend this game to anyone, new or veteran to the series.

It has a lot of great features like ages, the combat, the city/town/specialist settlements, etc.

The game is TOO EASY. I've already beaten it twice on deity, and I am far from an expert at this series. It took me YEARS to beat civ 5 and 6 on deity. I even used AI enhancements to make them more aggressive, build more units, and settle faster. And yet I still find it to be no challenge.

This game needs another year of work. Hold off. Especially when they give these overpriced DLC's at release that gatekeep the best civilizations that used to be core to the experience.

I'm massively disapointed in Firaxis and the brand as a whole. Shame on you.
Hundreds of hours in Civ V and VI (and Revolution lol) and yet since this game released I've only put a little over 3 hours into this title. I think that says enough.
The worst Civ game to date. Somehow they didn't iterate the well like featured but instead threw in untested ideas and didn't innovate the game in any of the ways that could've improved the series.

A Civilization game finally worthy of the 2K banner:-
- Botched release, CHECK
- Feels like a step down from its predecessor, CHECK
- Overpriced DLCs with sparse content, CHECK
- Post-release scramble to fix the game and fall short again, CHECK
- Made me go back and play the older games in the series, and reminisce of a simpler time, CHECK

Still can't believe I paid full price for an unfinished "AAA" game severely lacking polish. There are plenty of reviews both for and against the new mechanics, but all said and done, I cannot recommend the game in its current state.

I've played Civ since the very first version. For Civ 7, the 1.3 release, marks a time where the game is starting to hit its stride. The issues at launch are gone and I like how the title is evolving and how the team working on Civ 7 listen to the community. Would recommend.

Brought this game on Sale, what a waste of money. Thought it might get a bit exciting but it’s true boredom. Can’t return as over 2 hours played. I might play it a bit more just to try and justify the £40 price tag, but I should have listened to the reviews.

Honestly this is growing on me, and I'm happy that they are putting some effort into it. C6 was pretty average at first too, but now we love it. This game has some really good feature and after taking a break from CIV and coming back to C7, I feel like i can appreciate them more.

games kinda bad friends have never played with me so wouldnt actually have a valid review

Well, I don’t know what to say, its not bad: I like how they address when civilizations emerge historically, I like how production is faster, I like that you can rank up leaders. I don’t like… how continents STILL look like squares, how unartistic this game is with city building despite what they have added, how little you can customize the game/world, the fact that map sizes only go to standard(?!), the feeling that this game feels reliant on future DLC’s, there are no scenarios or a campaign, 
I know I haven’t spent a lot of time playing this game, BUT it’s clear that this game is a disappointment. It has less information/data, its slower pace & less variable, there are only a handful of leaders, and our existence is summed up in three ages; compared to the last edition (CIV 6). I would want my money back if I wasn’t bound to eventually purchase this game again; in hope that the next edition will build on its past and not bypass the continuing problems with playability, variability, immersion, and DEPTH.

The best strategy game released for PC since Age of Empires 4. I typically enjoy Civ titles, and this is the best Civ title released. Warning, it has a steep learning curve, and its not a game for idiots or the faint of heart. If you want a game that requires true strategy & tactics to win, and feels rewarding when your victorious, look no further.

What a disappointment. After investing hundreds of hours into this game, I’ve come to the disappointing realisation that I was fooling myself into thinking it was great. In truth, I was in denial, unwilling to admit that the developers had taken it in a direction that simply doesn’t work.

The introduction of the era system feels like a forced gimmick, likely designed to justify selling a “new” experience. But in practice, it resets the entire game every time, stripping away the sense of progression that makes strategy games so rewarding. The constant shift in leaders and civilisations feels arbitrary and breaks immersion. Many buildings feel pointless to construct because their value quickly becomes obsolete in the next era.

I could go on for pages about what’s wrong, but honestly, I’d rather not waste more time. I’ve gone back to playing Civ 6, which is vastly superior in terms of depth and replayability.

The only thing this game truly excels at is its visuals. It’s absolutely stunning. But beautiful graphics can’t save a broken design.

The game doesn't even feel like civilization anymore, the age transitions are dumb, the urban sprawl making the map unreadable is lame. Makes me miss civ 2, the game doesn't feel epic at all just speed run building something on one city. The game seems years away from ready.
Just fresh installed the game/Deluxe Edition, and it literally crashes every time I try to run a game. I'm trying some workarounds, but a $80 game shouldn't have these issues.
The best civilization version in many years. I'm finding myself enjoying this and getting sucked in to playing for several hours at a time.

I recently fired this game back up after some time away (March 2026, a little over a year after launch) to see if it had gotten any better and I am sad to report that it has not. I LOVED civs 5 and 6 and I've tried really hard (200+ hrs hard) to like this one but it's just not fun. The mechanics are tedious and the leader/civ abilities are way less fun and interesting than previous entries. I'm also still running into some of the same bugs I experienced at launch.

I think I'm gonna have to pack it in for good on this one bros

reason.text: Negative reviews focus on content that was cut and then sold as DLC, and on DLC priced too aggressively for the content offered.
Some reviews also say the game launched in a beta state missing basic features, and news reports from the same weeks describe a free update and DLC.

lines.F2: Sep 2026: 31% positive across 1,982 reviews (1,363 negative), against a usual 52% positive and 259 negative a month
lines.R3: (negative review, 781h played) "The game suffers from corporate greed. It was released in a beta state essentially at launch, missing basic features such as a finished UI. While continued updates add to the playability of the game, DLC is priced too aggressively for the amount of..."

lines.R14: (negative review, 19h played) "I love it when developers remove basic content that was in previous games to resell it to me again!"

tldr.text: Mixed (50%): players like the gameplay and combat and the ongoing updates.
The price and monetization draw the most complaints, while bugs and crashes also draw criticism.

details.text: A review bomb in September pulled the monthly score down to 31%, against a usual 52%, so that month was far below normal.
Players who have just started are much less positive than those who have put in many hours.
